Locate points in a triangle mesh

Source: R/cdt.R
cdt_locate.Rd

Find the triangle that contains each query point. This is the point locator inside cdt_interpolate() (a uniform grid of triangle buckets), with exact orientation tests from the bundled robust predicates, so a point is never lost to rounding between two triangles. With a triangle to feature table it answers point-in-polygon for many points at once.

Usage

cdt_locate(P, T, xq, yq, barycentric = FALSE)

Arguments

P

vertex coordinates (n x 2)

T

triangle vertex indices (m x 3, 1-based)

xq, yq

query coordinates

barycentric

if TRUE, return a data frame with the barycentric coordinates, rather than only the triangle index

Value

by default an integer vector, length(xq), of 1-based row indices into T (NA outside the mesh). With barycentric = TRUE, a data frame with one row per query point and columns triangle (the same index), and b1, b2, b3, which are NA where triangle is.

Details

A point on an edge or vertex shared by several triangles is given to the lowest triangle index that contains it. Points outside every triangle, and NA points, give NA. Triangles may be in either orientation, and degenerate (zero area) triangles contain no point.

With barycentric = TRUE the barycentric coordinates of each point in its triangle are returned as well. They are the weights of the triangle's three vertices (in the order given in T) that reproduce the point, so b1 * P[T[i, 1], ] + b2 * P[T[i, 2], ] + b3 * P[T[i, 3], ] is the point, and any per-vertex value is interpolated by the same weights, as cdt_interpolate() does. The weights are not negative and sum to 1; they are computed in double precision, with rounding error clamped, so a point on an edge has a weight of exactly 0 for the opposite vertex.

Examples

P <- cbind(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1))
T <- rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 3, 4))
## (0.5, 0.5) is on the shared diagonal: the lower triangle id wins
cdt_locate(P, T, xq = c(0.75, 0.25, 0.5, 2), yq = c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 2))
#> [1]  1  2  1 NA

## the weights of each triangle's vertices
loc <- cdt_locate(P, T, xq = c(0.75, 0.25, 0.5), yq = c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5),
                  barycentric = TRUE)
loc
#>   triangle   b1   b2   b3
#> 1        1 0.25 0.50 0.25
#> 2        2 0.25 0.25 0.50
#> 3        1 0.50 0.00 0.50
## a value known at the vertices, interpolated with those weights
z <- c(0, 10, 20, 10)
rowSums(as.matrix(loc[c("b1", "b2", "b3")]) * matrix(z[T[loc$triangle, ]], ncol = 3))
#> [1] 10 10 10
